forecaster_note: Evening refresh — today is done, so everything below is pointed at your next paddle. A messy mix of E/ESE windswell (3.9ft @ 9s) and leftover S windswell (2.8ft @ 8s) kept energy high today at 150 kJ, but a 13 km/h ENE onshore chopped it up all afternoon. Wednesday morning is the standout: a light W/NW offshore holds from dawn until roughly 9–10am with 118 kJ still in the water and a slightly better ENE (78°) angle, so the banks that were closing out today should have shape. It goes onshore ESE by lunchtime, so it's an early one. Then the tap turns off — Saturday is near flat (12 kJ, shin-high) before a new S groundswell with a 17s long-period component rebuilds Sunday to ~71 kJ. — Surf Guru agent summary, built from live Surfline forecast data.

wind.summary: Wednesday dawn: light W offshore 7 km/h gusting 14 — clean until about 9–10am, then swings ESE onshore 5–14 by midday.

days.label: Today
days.note: Day's over — last light was 5:53pm. Plenty of energy (150 kJ) but a 13 km/h ENE onshore ran all day, so it was fair-at-best and wind-affected. Long Reef held the size best at chest-to-head.

swells.label: S windswell — wraps poorly into the corner

dee-why.window: Gone. The 6–8am window was the only semi-clean patch (ENE only 6 km/h) before the sea breeze took over.
alerts: S 170° component wraps badly here — most of the size sat at Long Reef and Curl Curl instead

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: 150 kJ is a genuinely energetic day, but the ENE onshore meant the Point never lined up. When you get E 100° @ 9s with a light offshore, that's your frontside right — worth setting an alarm for a repeat.

swells.label: S windswell — Long Reef's best angle

long-reef.window: Pick of the four today — the headland shelters the ENE, so it was cross rather than straight onshore.

tip.label: Size winner
tip.text: Chest-to-head while Dee Why sat thigh-high — that's the S 170° component doing the work. Anytime you see S windswell in the mix, Long Reef is the call.

curl-curl.window: Early only — straight ENE onshore from about 8am on.

tip.label: Middle ground
tip.text: Solid size but fully exposed to the ENE. Curl Curl needs the wind under about 10 km/h to be worth the drive past Dee Why.

manly.window: Skip — smallest and windiest of the four.

tip.label: Backside lefts
tip.text: North Steyne shadows both swell angles today. Nothing here that Dee Why or Long Reef didn't do better.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The session of the week. Light W offshore at dawn (7 km/h), 118 kJ still running, and a cleaner ENE 78° angle. Clean until roughly 9–10am, onshore ESE by midday — so it's dawn-to-9:30, not your usual 10–12 mid-morning.

dee-why.window: Dawn (6:31am sunrise) to about 9:30am. ENE 78° is right in Dee Why's sweet spot and the W offshore should groom it — best combination you've had in a week.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: ENE 78° at 7–10s with a W offshore is exactly the setup that lights up the Point. 118 kJ is enough push for a proper session — go early, low tide is 6:10am so the bank should be working on the push.

long-reef.window: Dawn to mid-morning, offshore holds a bit longer here. Biggest of the four again.

tip.label: If you want size
tip.text: Chest-to-head with an offshore is the biggest clean surf on offer this week. Triple-swell mix (ENE 78°, ESE 110° @ 10s, SSE 157°) means it'll be a bit lumpy — but plenty to work with.

curl-curl.window: Dawn to about 9am — offshore goes cross-shore then onshore earlier here than at Long Reef.

tip.label: Punchy option
tip.text: Waist-to-chest with morning offshore is close to your favourite formula. If the Dee Why banks look sectiony from the carpark, Curl Curl is the backup.

manly.window: Dawn to 9am. Fine if you're already south, not worth the drive.

tip.label: Backside lefts
tip.text: North Steyne banks pick up the ESE 110° @ 10s better than the ENE. Smallest of the four but the cleanest water.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Two very different days. Saturday is near flat — 12 kJ, shin-to-knee, not worth waxing up. Sunday rebuilds to 71 kJ on a S 183° groundswell with a 17s long-period component, offshore SW at dawn. Sunday mid-morning is your weekend session.

dee-why.window: Skip Saturday entirely (12 kJ, NW offshore over nothing). Sunday 9am–12pm works — your preferred mid-morning slot for once.
alerts: Sunday's main swell is S 183° — dead south wraps badly into Dee Why, expect it to under-deliver vs Long Reef

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: Sunday's 1.4ft @ 17s S groundswell will show in sets but 183° is the angle that disappoints here. The 1.8ft ENE 59° secondary is what'll actually break on the bank — patchy, so pack patience.

long-reef.window: Sunday 9am–12pm, offshore all morning. Best weekend option by a clear margin.

tip.label: Weekend pick
tip.text: S 183° @ 9s plus a 17s long-period pulse is Long Reef's exact swell window, and the wind is offshore right through the morning. Waist-to-chest and clean — this is the one to plan around.

curl-curl.window: Sunday morning to about 11am before it goes cross-shore. Solid fallback if Long Reef is crowded.

tip.label: Backup plan
tip.text: Rated fair right through Sunday, which is the most consistent rating of the four. Picks up the S swell better than Dee Why without the Long Reef crowd.

tip.label: Backside lefts
tip.text: The S 183° swell is heavily shadowed by North Head down here. Head north for the weekend.
